item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is preferable because it verifies multipart correctness, validation, and—most importantly—the full uploaded payload on every retry. Both patches violate the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add and both omit a source-reader-error test.","reasons":["A's multipart test precisely parses the media type and verifies the field name, filename, and content.","A's retry test enables RetryAllMethods, matching the reported POST-upload configuration, and confirms the multipart payload remains intact on both attempts.","A tests empty-filename and nil-content validation before any request is made; B has no validation test.","A validates before constructing file options, while B unnecessarily processes options first."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of calling Add as the frozen contract requires.","It lacks the required test proving source-reader errors are propagated.","Its retry input is a bytes.Reader rather than an explicitly non-seekable streamed reader, although checking the encoded request on both attempts still provides useful replay coverage for the generated body worker."],"risks_b":["Upload also duplicates Add rather than routing through it.","The retry test neither sets RetryAllMethods nor reads the request body, so it does not directly demonstrate the reported POST configuration or body replay.","It lacks validation tests and a source-reader-error test."]}
